..
Super Typhoon Bavi continues to barrel toward the Marianas this
evening with the onset of damaging winds expected within the next 
couple of hours. Conditions will continue to deteriorate thereafter.
For additional information on Super Typhoon Bavi please see the 
Tropical Systems section. Shower and thunderstorm coverage will 
continue to increase as Bavi continues to trek to the west-northwest 
with widespread, heavy showers and scattered thunderstorms 
anticipated overnight. Scattered to numerous, locally heavy, showers 
throughout the day have helped to moisten soils and infiltration 
capacity may be limited in some areas to handle additional rainfall. 
Any additional infiltration capacity will be quickly overwhelmed in 
training showers and thunderstorms. Localized flooding will be 
possible this evening and overnight.

Tropical Systems...
A Typhoon Warning remains in effect for the Marianas as Super
Typhoon Bavi (09W) continues its approach. Bavi is moving west-
northwest at 10 mph and is expected to make passage through the 
southern Marianas beginning around mid-Monday morning, likely at 
Category 5 strength. It is expected to continue toward the west-
northwest and gradually increase in forward speed through Monday.
Surface observations across the Marianas show sustained winds around
25 mph with frequent tropical storm force gusts exceeding 40 mph, 
and the onset of sustained tropical storm force conditions is 
expected within the next hour or two. The latest forecast track
shifts the passage of Bavi slightly farther north, somewhere between
Rota and Tinian, but there is still time for the track to shift 
farther north or south. All islands will experience impacts. At 
minimum, damaging tropical storm force conditions are expected, but 
damage will be catastrophic near the center of Super Typhoon Bavi, 
with maximum sustained winds forecast at 175 mph at time of passage 
Monday morning. Significant flooding from torrential rains, and 
coastal inundation are expected. Surf will become extremely dangerous
ahead of Bavi's approach, potentially reaching 35 feet Monday. 
Significant coastal inundation and erosion are expected, with storm 
surge reaching 6 to 9 feet near the storm center with 10 to 15 feet 
of wind- and wave-driven runup.

For the islands closest to passage of Super Typhoon Bavi, the 
onset of typhoon conditions is expected Monday morning just ahead
of Bavi's center, continuing through Monday afternoon. Destructive
typhoon conditions may be expected for 8 to 10 hours close to the
center's passage, depending on forward speed.

For further information on Super Typhoon Bavi, see the Tropical
Cyclone Warnings issued by the Joint Typhoon Warning Center under WMO
header WTPN31 PGTW and the Tropical Cyclone Public Advisories issued
by the National Weather Service under WMO header WTPQ31 PGUM.

Eastern Micronesia...
Expect continued isolated to scattered showers and isolated 
thunderstorms through much of the week. Periods of scattered showers 
and isolated thunderstorms will continue this week as Kosrae remains 
in the vicinity of convergence along the Near-Equatorial Trough 
(NET). Mostly drier weather is expected at Majuro this week with only
isolated to low-end scattered showers and isolated thunderstorms 
expected. Though, a weak disturbance may bring periods of higher-end 
scattered showers as it drifts to the southwest through Monday.

Seas consist of a west-northwest swell emanating from Super Typhoon 
Bavi for Pohnpei and Kosrae and an east swell around Majuro. A small,
southerly swell is also present at all sites. An elevated surf 
threat is expected at Pohnpei along west-facing reefs into the first 
half of this week, headlines for the potential elevated surf 
continue. 

Western Micronesia...
Advisories for Chuuk. A Small Craft Advisory and a High Surf 
Advisory remain in effect.

Chuuk is in the westerly inflow notch of Super Typhoon Bavi. Expect 
fresh with near-gale gusts and elevated seas through Monday night. 
While in this notch showers are expected to be numerous tonight, and 
will taper down as Bavi moves into the Philippine Sea. Seas may 
return to below hazardous conditions as early as Tuesday.

Weather conditions over Yap and Palau will change as Bavi moves into
the Philippine Sea. Sea and surf conditions are expected to breach 
advisory criteria levels around Monday for Yap and Monday night for 
Palau. For now, weather conditions are deteriorating for the eastern 
islands in Yap and shower and thunderstorm trends will increase over 
the central and western islands through Monday as Bavi passes to the 
north. Once these conditions set in they are anticipated to linger 
through at least Thursday.
